entries.definition: being or producing something like nothing done or experienced or created before
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval that lands on the making: not simply that a thing is unprecedented but that someone brought something unprecedented about.
examples: innovative members of the artistic community

entries.definition: original and of a kind not seen before
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest way to make the claim - a thing is original and unlike anything seen before - with almost no approval loaded onto it.

entries.definition: original and of a kind not seen before
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cooler and more formal than *fresh*, treating the unlikeness to anything before as a fact worth remarking rather than a pleasure.
examples: the computer produced a completely novel proof of a well-known theorem

entries.definition: being or productive of something fresh and unusual; or being as first made or thought of
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Does double duty - mild approval for something fresh and unusual, and a flat statement that a thing stands as first made or thought of.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The flattest of the three: it credits the power to start something without *germinal*'s picture of a seed and its growth.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The heaviest praise here, treating the thing as the source everything afterwards grows out of - a standing *germinal* only promises.
examples: seminal ideas of one discipline can influence the growth of another

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise made by subtraction: it clears a thing of owing itself to a source and of copying a model, without claiming freshness the way *original* does.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemning: the country's superiority held as an article of faith, all conviction and no judgement.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mocks the display rather than the belief, reducing the fanaticism to noisy show where *chauvinistic* attacks the conviction behind it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The sharpest edge in the group, hearing the fanaticism as belligerence rather than mere excess of zeal.

entries.definition: inspired by love for your country
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Casts the same love as steadfast attachment rather than ardour, quieter and less demonstrative than *patriotic*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The coolest-sounding of the fanatical set, naming the excess as a doctrine where *flag-waving* names its noise.

entries.definition: inspired by love for your country
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain approving word for love of country, holding the feeling at a warmth that *jingoistic* has already burned past.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sarcastic: patriotism inflated past the point of belief, so the swelling itself is the accusation.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pushed past *nationalistic* to an extremity that leaves no reading in which the word admires what it describes.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Makes long duration sound like constancy, where *enduring* makes it sound like resistance.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Lofty and bookish — endlessness stated in the grandest available terms with no judgement attached to it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The one admiring member here — it presents going on indefinitely as something to be envied rather than merely measured, unlike *perpetual*.
examples: the ageless themes of love and revenge

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Long duration framed as strength, as though the thing had to hold out to reach it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries the same elevated, uncommitted weight as *aeonian*, adding nothing and softening nothing.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Solemn and absolute — it makes endlessness a property of the thing rather than a stretch of time, and still approves of nothing.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer than *eternal* — the endlessness sounds like something held onto rather than a fact declared.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest of the long-lasting three: not holding out like *enduring* but beyond decay altogether, which treats what it names as worth keeping.

entries.definition: continuing or enduring without marked change in status or condition or place
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Softer than *permanent* — duration sounds like something the thing has rather than a status fixed onto it.

entries.definition: continuing or enduring without marked change in status or condition or place
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and factual — the bare statement that a condition holds, without the warmth *lasting* can pick up.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Endlessness as plain mechanism, running on without the grandeur *eternal* brings to the same span.

entries.definition: not created for a particular occasion
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Positional rather than evaluative — it marks a thing as kept ready for whatever comes instead of raised for one occasion.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Presses on the missing pause, so what continues indefinitely reads as relentless rather than simply long.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames going on forever as the absence of any stop, which makes it sound wearing where *everlasting* makes it sound treasured.

entries.definition: not suitable or right or appropriate
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest disapproval here - it marks a thing as not fitting without naming the standard it fails, where *unseemly* and *indecent* both point at one.
examples: slightly improper to dine alone with a married man
improper attire for the golf course

entries.definition: not in accord with established usage or procedure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Cooler and more technical than *wrong* - the same failure to accord with established procedure, stated as a matter of record.
examples: it is incorrect for a policeman to accept gifts

entries.definition: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and severe where *indecorous* is measured - the same breach of what polite society accepts, named with nothing held back.

entries.definition: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and cool, faulting the breach as a lapse of decorum rather than an outrage, which is exactly where it parts from *indecent*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mild in shape but broad in reach - it runs from merely improper right through to offensive, and the understatement is what makes the far end land.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The spaced spelling carries the same span, improper at its softest and offensive at its hardest, with no more heat in it than *out-of-the-way*.

entries.definition: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Measures the breach against whoever commits it - the conduct falls below what suits them, where *indecorous* faults the conduct alone.

entries.definition: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faint and formal - it registers the breach of accepted standards as unattractive rather than shocking, staying well back from *indecent*.

entries.definition: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Firm and plain-spoken: the conduct does not fit at all, which is more pointed than *indecorous* and less scandalized than *indecent*.

entries.definition: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most restrained of this set, glancing at the breach rather than rebuking it as *unseemly* does.
examples: moved to curb their untoward ribaldry

entries.definition: not in accord with established usage or procedure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a measure against established usage or procedure - it records a mismatch rather than passing judgement, which is what separates it from *improper*.
examples: the wrong way to shuck clams

entries.definition: causing or tending to cause anger or resentment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The participle keeps the effect live - anger and resentment being stirred now, where *agitative* states a settled property.

entries.definition: causing or tending to cause anger or resentment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flat and clinical for what it describes, labelling a thing as anger-producing by disposition rather than catching the anger or resentment in the act.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The disturbance is set before you as something to be met, so the discomfort arrives with a demand attached rather than a verdict.

entries.definition: capable of producing violent emotion or arousing controversy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names a load waiting to go off, the violent feeling or the controversy stored in the thing and not yet released, where *inflammatory* names something already doing the work.
examples: the highly charged issue of abortion

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the image of a fire set on purpose, so stirring people to act or to rise is treated as damage waiting to happen.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A bare, near-technical label for the same power to move people to action or revolt, with none of the heat *incendiary* puts under it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heat is the whole point - it treats the thing as what sets the action or the rebellion alight, not merely the occasion for it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Points past the blaze to the hand behind it, naming what starts the action or the rising rather than how fiercely it burns.
